name: What is the difference between moving plumbing and replacing fixtures in a bathroom?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between moving plumbing and replacing fixtures in a bathroom?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between moving plumbing and replacing fixtures in a bathroom?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing bathroom fixtures is not the same as moving plumbing. Fixture replacement keeps the existing water and drain locations and simply swaps the visible product, such as a new toilet, faucet, sink, or shower trim. Plumbing relocation changes the hidden pipe routes so the fixture itself can sit in a new position. That means more demolition, rough plumbing, inspection, and reconstruction. The difference matters because homeowners often request a “simple replacement” when the project really involves structural and drain-line changes. A new toilet at the same location is very different from shifting that toilet across the room. The same is true for a vanity versus a shower pan. If the goal is mainly style or finish improvement, replacing fixtures may be enough. If the goal is improving layout, traffic flow, or accessibility, plumbing relocation is usually required and should be planned as a separate scope.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replacing fixtures means installing new sinks, toilets, or faucets in the same locations. Moving plumbing means rerouting supply, drain, and vent lines so those fixtures can be installed in a different place, which is more invasive and expensive.
